stem: An adult with sepsis initially receives broad empiric antimicrobial therapy. Culture and susceptibility results later identify one susceptible bacterial pathogen. Which change best reflects current antimicrobial de-escalation guidance?

options.A: Discontinue unnecessary agents or narrow the regimen to therapy directed at the identified susceptible pathogen.
options.B: Continue every empiric antimicrobial for the full course even when culture data show that several agents are unnecessary.
options.C: Broaden therapy further after susceptibility results identify a narrower active option.
options.D: Ignore microbiology results because de-escalation is recommended only when cultures remain negative.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommends antimicrobial de-escalation when a confirmed microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available. The guideline defines de-escalation as discontinuing unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or narrowing the spectrum when appropriate. B and C do the opposite of de-escalation. D is incorrect because the strongest de-escalation recommendation specifically applies when microbiologic diagnosis and susceptibility are available; the guideline also separately suggests de-escalation in selected culture-negative cases.
educational_objective: When microbiology identifies a susceptible pathogen in sepsis, support antimicrobial de-escalation by discontinuing unnecessary agents or narrowing therapy rather than continuing avoidable broad empiric coverage.
source_organization: Society of Critical Care Medicine / European Society of Intensive Care Medicine, Surviving Sepsis Campaign
source_document_title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
source_locator: Antimicrobial Therapy recommendation: for adults with sepsis or septic shock, recommend de-escalation over no de-escalation when a confirmed microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available. Remarks: de-escalation involves discontinuing unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or narrowing antimicrobial spectrum where appropriate. Separate conditional recommendation supports de-escalation even when no pathogens are identified on final cultures.
source_claim_supported: Current adult sepsis guidance recommends antimicrobial de-escalation after microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility data, using discontinuation of unnecessary agents or spectrum narrowing as appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: support evidence-based infection management and practices that reduce avoidable antimicrobial exposure and infection-related risk.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — antimicrobial de-escalation
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item around the newly current 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign definition of de-escalation. Removed the stronger unsupported causal claim that narrowing therapy itself necessarily reduces resistance development in the individual case and instead tests the exact guideline action: stop unnecessary agents or narrow spectrum using culture/susceptibility data.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against the March 2026 SSC adult guideline's explicit antimicrobial de-escalation recommendation and definition.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A exactly states the guideline-defined action. B continues unnecessary therapy. C broadens despite narrower susceptibility-guided treatment. D falsely limits de-escalation to negative cultures.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; stop unnecessary agents or narrow spectrum.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; de-escalation is strongly recommended when microbiology and susceptibility are confirmed.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches the guideline definition; the stem supplies the microbiological condition required for the recommendation.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are competing antimicrobial changes after results return.
audit_findings.blueprint: Stewardship within infection management fits Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked culture-positive versus culture-negative guidance and removed unsupported guarantees about resistance outcomes. No second defensible answer remained.
